---
title: "FIR crossings"
description: "How OPDI finds each passage of a flight from one flight information region to another (xing-fir)."
---

## In one sentence

An `xing-fir` event marks each moment a flight passes from one flight
information region (FIR), or upper information region (UIR), to another.

## What it needs

- The FIR and UIR volumes of the EUROCONTROL Network Manager airspace model,
  for AIRAC cycle 524 (valid 2024-11-28 to 2024-12-26). An **AIRAC cycle** is
  the 28-day period in which aeronautical data such as airspace boundaries
  take effect. Each volume has a lateral boundary and a lowest and highest
  flight level.
- The cleaned positions and barometric altitudes of the track's reports.

## How it is computed

1. **Grid.** Before any flight is processed, every volume is filled with H3
   cells: as small as resolution 7 (about 5 km² each) along the boundaries,
   larger inside.
2. **Lookup.** Each report whose position survived cleaning is placed in the
   volume whose cells contain its position and whose flight-level band
   contains its altitude. Where two volumes overlap, the one with the
   narrowest level band wins, then the one with the smallest area.
3. **Short stays.** A stay in one volume shorter than 60 s is counted as part
   of the volume before it, so a flight along a boundary does not cross it at
   every cell.
4. **Crossing.** A crossing is a change of volume between two consecutive
   stays. A stretch with no volume in between (for example where the altitude
   was removed by cleaning) does not count as leaving and entering again. The
   event sits on the first report in the new volume.
5. A crossing whose two reports imply more than 1,000 kt (a position that
   jumped) is not given.
6. `info.vertical` is true when the two volumes lie one above the other (their
   flight-level bands do not overlap), as a FIR and the UIR above it: the
   crossing is then a climb or descent through the boundary level, not a
   lateral crossing.

Nothing is computed across a reception gap of more than 30 minutes kept
inside a track.

## Based on

The volumes are those of the EUROCONTROL Network Manager airspace model. The
grid is [H3](https://h3geo.org/). The lookup and the rules of steps 3 to 6
were developed for OPDI; see
[Holding, point merge and FIR crossings as flight events](../../papers/airspace-events-v1/index.html).

## What is published

Event type `xing-fir`, with position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and
`time_passed_s`. Its `info` holds `crossing_seq`, `fir_from`, `fir_to`, `fl`,
`bracket_s`, `airac_cfmu` (524), `airac_validity_start`,
`airac_validity_end` and `vertical` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Flights and distance per region**: the difference of `distance_flown_nm`
  between two consecutive crossings of a flight is the distance flown in one
  region.
- **Traffic entering a region per hour**, for example to compare with
  capacity.
- **Lateral crossings only**: leave out the crossings with `info.vertical`
  true.

## Limitations

The same AIRAC cycle is used for every day, so a boundary changed since then
is not followed. See
[Limitations: FIR crossings](../limitations.qmd#lim-fir).

## Availability and accuracy

Not compared with flight records: the Network Manager's records of region
crossings could not be used. The study below checks the grid lookup against
the exact boundaries of the same regions, which tests the method but not
